raw_text:
Below is a focused 3-week peaking block designed to take an intermediate female lifter into a powerlifting meet 21 days away. Goal: preserve and reinforce heavy intensities (neural readiness), progressively reduce volume to promote recovery and freshness, keep technical practice and confidence on competition lifts (squat, bench, deadlift), and include brief accessory work to maintain muscle balance and feel-good durability. You said last 12 weeks of accumulation are done, so I’ll assume she’s been working near meet intensities and is generally healthy. This plan assumes a full gym is available and that she’ll compete raw with single-ply or raw rules (adjust if using briefs/equipment).

General principles used
- Intensity (% of 1RM or RPE) largely maintained or slightly reduced to keep CNS primed; volume (sets x reps) progressively tapers.
- Heavy singles at ~92–98% will be used early in the block, with final week staying sharp but not grinding heavy 1RMs.
- Emphasis on competition variants (competition-style squat, paused bench, conventional or sumo deadlift depending on her meet style), with technique cues and opener/second/third attempt rehearsals.
- Accessory work is light and targeted for mech. efficiency and recovery: mobility, glute/horizontal/back support, rotator cuff, core.
- Two to four training days per week depending on her current schedule; below I present a 4-day option (common for intermediate lifters). If she only trains 3 days, we can combine or remove one accessory day.
- Nutrition: maintain calories at roughly maintenance to slight + for recovery early in block, then maintain maintenance or slight surplus early after heavy sessions; prioritize protein and carbs around workouts. Meet day: carbohydrate loading in the 24–36 hours before, hydration, and sodium as needed.
- Recovery: sleep 8+ hours, prioritize mobility, short walks, contrast showers/sauna if used, and avoid new stressing activities. Reduce high-intensity cardio. Avoid heavy squats or maximal deadlifts in the final week.

Notation for intensities
- % of estimated 1RM (if she knows exact numbers use those). If she prefers RPE, target: heavy singles ~RPE 8–9 early, last week RPE 7–8 for openers.
- Reps and sets listed are general; warm-ups are not detailed but include progressive warm-up sets to target weight.

Schedule (4 training days/week): Day A — Heavy squat focus, Day B — Heavy bench focus, Day C — Light technique/accessory or active recovery (optional), Day D — Heavy deadlift + light bench/overhead. You can move days to fit meet timing so that the last heavy session is 5–6 days before the meet (we’ll arrange the final heavy to be 6 days out, with two light sessions in the last 5 days).

Week 1 (Days 21–15 before meet) — Heavy, but controlled
Goal: maintain heavy intensity, establish singles at >90%, start reducing volume.

Day 1 — Heavy Squat + Accessories
- Competition-style Squat: Work up to 2 singles at 92–94% 1RM (or RPE 8–9). Keep depth and tempo competition-like.
- Backoff: 2 sets x 3 reps @ ~82–85% (or RPE 7) — controlled but not grinding.
- Pause squat or box squat: 2 x 3 @ ~70% (focus on pause and position).
- Bulgarian split squat (DB): 3 x 6–8 each leg (light–moderate) — for single-leg control.
- Ab/core: 3 x 12-15 weighted plank variations or anti-extension work.
- Mobility: 10 minutes hip/ankle mobility.

Day 2 — Heavy Bench + Light Accessories
- Competition-style Bench: Work up to 2 singles at 92–95% 1RM (paused if that’s her meet style). Focus on groove and tightness.
- Backoff: 2 x 3 @ ~80–85% (control).
- Close-grip bench or paused incline: 2 x 5 @ 65–70% (technique and triceps strength).
- Row variation (barbell or chest-supported): 3 x 8–10 (maintain upper back strength).
- Rotator cuff/facepulls: 3 x 12–15.
- Mobility: pec/shoulder mobility and thoracic extension.

Day 3 — Optional Active Recovery / Mobility
- Light conditioning: 20–30 min walk or very light bike.
- Movement prep: light goblet squats, band pull-aparts.
- Foam rolling and targeted mobility.

Day 4 — Heavy Deadlift + Light Bench/Accessories
- Deadlift (competition style): Work up to 2 singles at 92–95% 1RM (or RPE 8–9). These should be crisp, not grinders.
- Backoff: 2 x 3 @ ~80–85% (speed/position).
- Romanian deadlifts or stiff-leg: 2 x 6–8 @ moderate load (focus hamstring).
- Pull-ups or lat pulldown: 3 x 6–8.
- Farmer carry or heavy carry: 3 x 30–60s.
- Core: 3 x anti-rotation chops or Pallof presses.

Notes Week 1: Keep all “heavy” singles crisp and stop short of failure. Sleep and nutrition slightly above maintenance on heavy days; ensure good carbs pre- and post-workout.

Week 2 (Days 14–8 before meet) — Taper volume, maintain intensity but fewer sets/reps
Goal: fewer sets, keep single intensity similar or slightly lower, rehearse openers and second attempts.

Day 1 — Squat Focus
- Competition Squat: Work up to 1–2 singles at 90–93% (choose crisp weights; these can be scheduled as opener and planned 2nd).
- Backoff: 1 x 3 @ 80% (or 1 x 2 @ 82%).
- Light paused squat or tempo: 2 x 3 @ 60–65% (technique only).
- Short accessory: 2 x 8 split squats, 2 x 12 ab work.
- Mobility: brief mobility and breathing drills.

Day 2 — Bench Focus
- Competition Bench: Work up to 1–2 singles at 90–93% (paused). Focus on perfect setup.
- Backoff: 1 x 3 @ ~78–82%.
- Light incline or close-grip: 2 x 5 @ 60–65%.
- Light rows + facepulls: 2 x 10 each.
- Rotator cuff prehab.

Day 3 — Light Recovery / Mobility or OFF
- Low-intensity movement, stretching, and short walks.
- Optional short session for technique: 2–3 paused bench singles at 50–60% focusing on groove.

Day 4 — Deadlift Focus + Light Bench
- Deadlift: 1–2 singles at ~90–93% (crisp). No heavy backoffs.
- Light Romanian or speed pulls: 2 x 3 @ 60–70% (explosive).
- Light bench volume: 2 x 3 @ ~60–65% (groove).
- Light accessory: 2 x 8 db rows, 2 x 12 core.
- Recovery: mobility and foam roll.

Notes Week 2: Volume is down ~40–50% from week 1. Emphasize sleep and carbohydrate intake the 48–72 hours before the meet (start carb timing ramp Wednesday/Thursday if meet is weekend). Continue walking and mobility. No sets to true failure.

Week 3 (Final Week — Days 7–0) — Peak, technical rehearsal, freshen up
Goal: be fresh and neurologically sharp. Practice openers and light technique only. Final heavy attempt simulation should happen no later than Day 6 before meet; otherwise this week is mostly light.

Recommended layout if meet on a Saturday (example):
- Monday (Day 7): Light technical session — opener rehearsals; short, sharp.
- Wednesday (Day 5): Brief session focusing bench or squat opener feel; no grinding.
- Friday (Day 2): Very light activation session (optional) or full rest and mobility.
- Meet Day (Day 0): Compete.

Detailed Week 3 plan

Day 1 (7 days out) — Short opener rehearsal (All lifts)
- Squat: 1–2 singles at 80–85% (opener weight). Focus setup, walkout, depth, and confidence.
- Bench: 1–2 singles at 80–85% (opener). Paused if appropriate — focus on setup and leg drive.
- Deadlift: 1 single at 80–85% (opener). Fast and technical; not maximal.
- Minimal accessories: short upper back and core work, e.g., 2 x 10 facepulls, 2 x 12 ab.
- Session length: 45–60 minutes; stop if fatigue accumulates.

Day 2 (5 days out) — Light tune-up (choose 1–2 lifts)
- If squats gave fatigue, do bench/dl tune-up; otherwise do bench + light squat.
- Bench: 2 singles at opener weight or 1–2 sets x 2 @ 60% — focus on groove.
- Deadlift: 1 single at opener or technique pulls 2 x 2 @ 60%.
- Mobility and short walk.

Day 3 (3–2 days out) — Mostly rest and mental prep
- Primarily rest. Short walk, mobility, mental visualization and attempt selection strategy.
- Pack meet bag, weigh-in plan, warm-up plan, and nutrition/hydration.
- Carb intake: maintain moderate-high carbs the 48 hours before meet; aim to top up glycogen without making her feel bloated. Example: normal carbs through Thursday, slightly higher carbs Friday if meet Saturday (pasta/rice and familiar foods).
- Hydration: maintain normal hydration; avoid excessive water load unless she’s manipulating weight.

Day 4 (Contest day or Day 0) — Meet
- Warm-up plan: follow normal meet warm-up progression; keep mental cues and avoid over-warming.
- Attempt selection: pick openers at a weight that is around 90–92% of recent training max or a weight she can hit confidently for a solid single. Second attempts should be a realistic increase (~97–99% depending on confidence). Third attempts should be an aggressive but realistic PR attempt; avoid surprise heavy attempts if it could cost placing.
- Nutrition on the day: breakfast 2–4 hours pre weigh-in and eat depending on weigh-in timing. Bring easily digestible carbs for between weigh-in and lifting: bananas, rice cakes, sports drink. Continue small sips of fluid and maintain electrolytes.
- Warm-up carbs: small simple-carb snacks between sessions (gels, fruit, cereal) to keep energy.

Accessory and recovery guidance for entire 3-week block
- Keep accessory intensity light-to-moderate; volume steadily decreases.
- Avoid introducing new lifts or heavy conditioning.
- Sleep target: 8+ hrs. If short on sleep, reduce accessory volume that day.
- Pain vs soreness: Manage acute pain with rest/physio. If joint pain flares, reduce intensity and consult medical professional.
- Deload caffeine/alcohol in the last 48 hours; avoid heavy alcohol at all in the last week.
- Use light massage, mobility, contrast shower, or sauna if they help recovery and are part of her normal routine.

Nutrition specifics (concise)
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight daily to maintain muscle and recovery.
- Calories: maintenance or slight surplus on heavy days early in block; overall maintain to prevent unnecessary weight changes.
- Carbs: prioritize around training: 60–90 minutes pre-workout carbs and 30–60 g simple carbs after heavy sessions.
- Sodium: ensure normal sodium intake; increase modestly pre-meet if risking low weight/fluids.
- Meet-day: eat familiar foods; avoid anything new. Keep snacks easy to digest and sugary carbs for quick energy between flights.

Sample opener/attempt planning (simple template)
- Opener: conservative, ~90–92% (comfortable single).
- Second: 97–99% or a 3–4% jump from opener depending on confidence.
- Third: Hinge on how second felt; could be 100%+ if going for PR, or a smaller jump if aiming for placement. Encourage coach/client discussion before each attempt.

Coaching cues and mental prep
- Rehearse walkouts, commands, and breathing under near-competition weight.
- Use short visualization sessions nightly in the final week: successful lifts, smooth setups, and managing nerves.
- Keep language positive; emphasize what the lifter can control: sleep, food, attempt selection, and technique.

If you want:
- I can convert these %s to concrete weights if you provide her current competition 1RMs (squat/bench/deadlift).
- Or I can shrink this to a 3-day/wk version if she prefers fewer sessions.
- Or give a day-by-day calendar aligned to her exact meet date (so the last heavy day is exactly 6 days out).

Good luck — she should go into the meet fresh, technically sharp, and primed to perform.
